races.paceDynamic: Ramon Di Loria will lead from the gates with his prominent style, setting a comfortable gallop that won't be pressured by the predominantly hold-up field behind him. Rain Cap may sit handy in second, but the overwhelming majority of runners including Rambuso Creek, Invincible Ruby, Sunlit Sea, Jack Rabbit Slims, Baby Rover, Wait For It and Flybar will settle in behind. With only two early pace angles, Ramon Di Loria gets an uncontested lead on soft ground over six furlongs. This race shape strongly favours the front two, particularly Ramon Di Loria who can dictate terms throughout.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Ramon Di Loria jumps cleanly and establishes his lead without interference.
scenarios.body: The 8-year-old gets first run on the field turning for home and his recent third at this course suggests he handles these conditions well. The hold-up brigade arrive too late to catch him.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Rally Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes too steady and the leaders stop.
scenarios.body: Rambuso Creek and Invincible Ruby benefit from a strong finish, with Tudhope's mount particularly dangerous given his recent Carlisle win. The soft ground helps their staying power in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Rain Cap travels easily in second and challenges Ramon Di Loria late.
scenarios.body: Both early runners have enough stamina for six furlongs and can kick clear of the hold-up horses. Rain Cap's fresh legs from a 70-day break could be decisive against the more exposed leader.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a crawl throughout.
scenarios.body: Sunlit Sea or Jack Rabbit Slims produce devastating late kicks from impossible positions. This requires the leaders to go too slow early and completely stop in front.

watchPoints.text: Ramon Di Loria's jump from the stalls - if he misses the break, the entire pace dynamic changes
Rain Cap's fitness levels after 70 days off - watch for early signs of rustiness or sharpness
Rambuso Creek in the market - significant support would suggest confidence after 4-day turnaround
Sunlit Sea's early positioning - Prescott runners often need the run first time back
Any hold-up horse showing early pace - would create pressure on Ramon Di Loria's lead

races.paceDynamic: With every runner showing hold-up style tendencies and no confirmed front-runner in this 9-horse field, the early pace will be pedestrian with the field bunching together through the first half of this 6f sprint. Howzak, April Diamond, and Great Success are most likely to drift forward early but none are natural pace-setters, creating a slow tempo that will compress the field. This crawling pace sets up a frantic sprint finish over the final 2f where position and turn of foot matter most. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can secure good position early and hold-up horses with proven acceleration, while penalising those who need genuine pace to aim at.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow early with no horse willing to make it a test
scenarios.body: The field will be tightly bunched turning for home creating a cavalry charge finish where the best horses on form with tactical speed will prevail. Maynora and Howzak benefit most from this compressed finish where class and recent winning form shine through.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Moderate Tempo Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If April Diamond or Great Success take the field along at a more sensible gallop
scenarios.body: This creates a more traditional sprint race where those with proven 6f form can show their true ability without getting caught in traffic. Maynora's recent soft ground win and Stormy Pearl's consistent 6f efforts come to the fore.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Pace Injection
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses make their move simultaneously in the final 2f creating a sustained drive
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure test of stamina and acceleration where horses who finish strongly over 6f will dominate. Howzak's course win and Great Success's best efforts when not fading benefit from this sustained finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Problems Decide
scenarios.trigger: If the slow pace creates a wall of horses turning in with several runners getting hampered
scenarios.body: Those drawn favourably or ridden with early tactical awareness avoid the carnage and benefit from others' misfortune. April Diamond and Belling The Cat could profit if others get into trouble behind horses.

watchPoints.text: Watch for traffic problems in the final 2f if Howzak, Great Success, and Stormy Pearl all make their moves simultaneously from similar positions
Monitor how quickly April Diamond and Maynora can secure good early position as their ability to avoid the inevitable traffic will be crucial
Observe if any runner shows more natural pace than expected early as this could completely change the race dynamic
Watch Great Success and Invincible Annice for signs of their usual late fade as both have shown this pattern recently
Check if the soft ground is riding slower than advertised as this would further compress the field and increase the lottery element

races.paceDynamic: So Alex stands alone as the confirmed front runner and will dictate proceedings from the off, likely getting an uncontested lead with Dance Time, Marbuzet and Trojan Sun settling in prominent positions behind. The lack of natural pace pressure means So Alex can control fractions and kick for home when ready, while the large field of hold-up horses including Gentle Warrior, Ouro Preto, Banderas and Torcello will need gaps and racing room in the straight. This tactical setup strongly favours prominent runners who can track the pace and those with proven finishing kicks from off the speed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Suits Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If So Alex gets uncontested fractions and Dance Time/Marbuzet track handily
scenarios.body: The pace-setter can dictate terms throughout while the prominent trackers get first run on the field. Hold-up horses face traffic problems in a large field with limited early pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Charge From Back
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop becomes truly dawdling and gaps open late
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace sets up a sprint finish where class tells and hold-up horses get clear runs. Fresh legs and higher ratings prove decisive in soft conditions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Division Moves Early
scenarios.trigger: If prominent horses make moves before the straight to avoid traffic
scenarios.body: Horses like Circuit Breaker and Clansman get competitive positions early and sustain their efforts. The large field creates a cavalry charge finish favouring those already in contention.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Suits Outsiders
scenarios.trigger: If So Alex stops quickly and chaos ensues in the straight
scenarios.body: The race becomes a lottery with interference and the longest-priced hold-up horses finding gaps others cannot. Fresh horses from impossible positions suddenly become live chances.

races.paceDynamic: Hostility and Bellasio will dispute early leadership with both showing prominent tendencies, creating a measured but honest gallop over this mile trip on testing ground. The lack of confirmed speed horses means the pace will be sustainable rather than fierce, allowing the large contingent of hold-up performers to get into contention. With 8 of the 12 runners preferring to come from behind, the early leaders face minimal pressure through the middle stages. This moderate tempo strongly favours the prominent runners who can position close to the pace without being asked hard questions early, as they'll have first run on a large field of closers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent pair dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Hostility and Bellasio dictate a steady tempo without interference
scenarios.body: The pace-setters maintain their advantage as the hold-up brigade leave their challenges too late on the testing ground. Bellasio's superior recent form and Hostility's consistency prove decisive when they have first run on the field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late surge succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes too steady and creates a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The large pack of hold-up horses gets into the race simultaneously, with Union Island's class and Soames Forsyte's fresh legs proving decisive. The testing conditions don't prevent a strong finish from those who conserve energy early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-division strike
scenarios.trigger: If prominent runners fade but hold-up horses are too far back
scenarios.body: Jewel Maker uses his experience to track the leaders before striking, while Between Me And U benefits from a perfect tracking position. Their tactical positioning proves superior to both the pace-setters and those held up too far.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider ambush
scenarios.trigger: If the field comes back to the tail-enders in testing conditions
scenarios.body: The soft ground becomes the great leveller as Betty Bassett and Jkr Cobbler benefit from light weights and patient rides. Their fresher legs prove telling in the final furlong as higher-rated rivals tire.

races.paceDynamic: Sandy Craic will likely take the field along from the front with Blufferonthebus and Velvet Rhythm sitting prominent, but this looks a manageable pace rather than a sprint. The majority of the field are hold-up types including Amelia's Joy, Sailor's Return, Pickersgill, Albeseeingyer, Douwantitrightnow and Sahara Magic, which should create a steady tempo early. With so many horses needing to be produced late, the race will develop into a sprint finish from the 2f pole. This race shape clearly favours the prominent racers and early pace-setters who can avoid the inevitable traffic problems.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Racers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Sandy Craic and the prominent runners control the tempo without burning up.
scenarios.body: The hold-up brigade get caught in traffic as the pace quickens late, while those racing handily avoid the scramble. Velvet Rhythm and Sandy Craic can dictate terms and prove hard to peg back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a cavalry charge.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy sprint with multiple horses trying to improve simultaneously from off the pace. Amelia's Joy and Sailor's Return benefit from their class and finishing kick when gaps appear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Blufferonthebus Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent duo go too fast and come back to the field.
scenarios.body: Sandy Craic and Velvet Rhythm set unsustainable fractions allowing the patient racers to pick up the pieces. Blufferonthebus can time his run perfectly from the ideal stalking position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If no one wants the lead and they crawl early before sprinting.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a 2f dash with horses fanned across the track in a blanket finish. Anorah Unleashed's light weight becomes crucial in a desperate scramble where anything can happen.

races.paceDynamic: The Gay Blade and Good Karma are the only two prominent runners in a field dominated by hold-up horses. The Gay Blade has been racing prominently and winning from forward positions, while Good Karma can also press the pace when needed. With six hold-up horses including Saisons d'Or, Lightning Galaxy, Lesley's Boy, Jamaican Storm, El Pinto and King Sharja all needing to come from behind, the early pace will be modest to steady. This tactical setup strongly favours the front-runners and prominent racers who can dictate terms and kick for home before the back-markers can mount their challenges.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If The Gay Blade and Good Karma can establish an uncontested lead without pressure
scenarios.body: They can dictate a steady tempo before quickening late, making it difficult for the hold-up brigade to close the gap in time. The prominent pair's recent form shows they can sustain their efforts when not pressured early.

scenarios.label: B

scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too slow and the field bunches up entering the straight
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get their ideal scenario with a sprint finish where class can tell. Jamaican Storm and Saisons d'Or have shown strong finishing kicks when getting the right race shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Compromise
scenarios.trigger: If Good Karma presses The Gay Blade creating a reasonable gallop throughout
scenarios.body: This creates the perfect scenario for a horse that can track the leaders and outstay them. Lesley's Boy's consistency at this trip suggests he could benefit from this tactical setup.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If both prominent runners go too slowly and kick too late allowing a wall of closers
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint where the strongest finisher prevails regardless of early position. Lightning Galaxy has shown glimpses of ability when getting the right conditions.
